correctness.rationale: The full coded language is fixed to factors of blocks \(0^r1^{kr}\). Explicit right and left completion constructions give lengths at most \(km\) and \(\lceil n/k\rceil+k-1\), for all admissible words including one-symbol and one-run boundary cases. Concatenating the completions at a generator boundary is valid. For \(m\ge2\), \(n\ge k+2\), \(t=\lfloor(n-2)/k\rfloor\), the concrete pair \(u=0^{m-1}1\), \(v=01^{kt}0^{n-kt-1}\) forces \(k(m-1)-1\) ones after u and \(t-1\) disjoint zeros preceding the first ones in v. The claimed \(w=1^{k(m-1)-1}0^{t-1}\) realizes the forced amount. Thus the two-sided bounds and uniform \(O_k(1)\) law hold without a computational assumption. The separately coded generator-cycle language checker passed 6234 pairwise construction tests, 132 extremal witness tests and 13901 shorter-bridge exclusions for small cases.

value.rationale: The minimum-bridge profile is an intrinsic, natural gluing invariant measuring the scale of specification failure, not a routine finite example. The theorem identifies two independently variable directional costs: coefficient k for the outgoing word and 1/k for the incoming word, including a uniform bounded error and a lower certificate whose bridge is exactly optimal for the displayed family. This adds structural content beyond qualitative transitivity and non-specification and gives constructive finite-word gluing bounds.
